$comment: PadStudio design tokens: the one source for the app (padstudio/app/.../ui/theme/Tokens.kt) and the HTML preview (docs/redesign/tokens.css). Plan §3.1 and §3.6; contract in docs/redesign/BRIEF.md, 'Token contract'.

Edit this file, then run `node padstudio/design/make_tokens.mjs`. It checks WCAG contrast for all ten schemes and writes both outputs only if every pair passes. `--check` verifies that the committed outputs are up to date.
Method: WiFiBar's Branding/make_android_colors.mjs with @material/material-color-utilities 0.3.0 (0.4.0 has a broken ESM import).

Primary and secondary come from SchemeFidelity on the seed, so primary-container is the seed itself unless the seed's tone is 50-59: Material avoids that 'awkward zone' by moving the container to tone 49 in light and 60 in dark (Ocean and Emerald).
Tertiary takes the hue and chroma of a second colour. Neutrals take the hue of #F5F5F7 at very low chroma; the neutral variant takes the seed's hue at chroma 6.
Background and surface are pinned to #F5F5F7 (light) and #1C1C1E (dark), with a hand-spaced surface-container ladder around them so cards stand off the background.

surfaces.$comment: A hex string pins the role; a number is that tone (0-100) of the neutral palette. Same ladder as WiFiBar: in light, white cards on #F5F5F7 and darker containers below it; in dark, lighter steps above #1C1C1E.

palettes.$comment: From Branding/probe/canvas.py PALETTES: seed = the gradient top (first colour), tertiary = the glow (third colour). Order here is the order of the BrandPalette enum. defaultPalette above is the app's palette until the logo pick chooses one (plan §3.1).

Graphite.$comment: Graphite's glow is pure white, which has no hue to borrow. #8A94A6 is a neutral cool grey (HCT hue 258, chroma 15). Material's own SchemeNeutral gives its tertiary chroma 16, so this is still 'neutral' by Material's definition. It is 21 degrees bluer than Graphite's violet-grey seed (hue 280, chroma 7), so tertiary accents stay distinguishable from primary while the scheme stays grey. Measured: with #8A94A6 the tertiary container is #414B5B against the primary container #4A4A52; with a chroma-10 grey (#8C919C) it was #464B55, within 4 RGB steps of it.

$comment: Separate from the brand. good and warn are fixed base colours, used as they are for tints and fills in both themes; 'bad' is each scheme's own error colour.

ink is the colour of status icons and short status labels; a theme without an entry uses the base colour. The bases are too light for icons on light surfaces (2.03:1 for good and 1.64:1 for warn on #F5F5F7, under WCAG's 3:1), so light themes use darker shades of the same colour: exactly the preview kit's light-mode inks, color-mix(in oklab, base 62% (good) or 55% (warn), black), which keeps each base's chromaticity. Dark themes keep the bases.
The generator gates every ink at 3:1 on its theme's background, surface and five surface containers.

type.$comment: sp at font scale 1.0 (1 sp = 1 px in the preview frame): size and line height. Android scales sp nonlinearly above 1.0; docs/redesign/fontscale.js mirrors AOSP's tables. labelSmall is the preview's 11/16 'label-small' role (the widget's app labels, plan §6b; captions and meta text), which fontscale.js already scales. Sized for the owner's tablet (font scale 1.25, Bold text; 12 Oct: 'ui feels too tight', 'decrease font size'): the nonlinear curve grows small text about 29 % there and 30 sp not at all, so a cut that looks even in sp barely shrinks body text on screen. At 1.25 these render 11-18 % smaller than round 2's first scale (30/24/18/15/15/13/12/11): body 16.5 dp, not 18.75. titleMedium and bodyMedium have their own roles.

weight.$comment: Body 400, titles 500, never above 600: the tablet's Bold text adds 300 to every weight. Emphasis comes from size and colour.

corner.$comment: Radii in dp. full is a pill: Compose clamps a radius to half the shorter side.

space.$comment: dp. Every value is a multiple of gridUnit (the generator checks it). Touch targets are at least 48 x 48 dp. Round 2: more air (gutter 32, card padding 24, gapM 20, gapL 32).
